planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Vera Jameson's low, sprawling stems make it better suited to a border edge or wall than the upright sedums it's often paired with.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun. Vera Jameson is a low, spreading sedum with smoky purple-gray succulent foliage on lax stems that sprawl outward rather than standing upright, topped in late summer by dusky rose-pink flower clusters that draw butterflies and bees. Its trailing habit makes it useful for softening the front of a border, tumbling over a low wall, or filling a container, where the dark foliage contrasts nicely against green-leaved neighbors. Like other sedums it thrives on neglect, needing no fertilizer and very little water once established, and can be divided every few years in spring if the clump gets thin in the center.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Brilliant is an older showy-stonecrop cultivar and a parent of the widely grown Autumn Joy hybrid group.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun. Brilliant forms tidy, upright clumps of pale gray-green succulent foliage topped from late summer into fall by broad, flat clusters of vivid rose-pink flowers that are noticeably brighter and clearer in color than the muddier tones of many later hybrids. Its sturdy stems stand well without staking and its flowers draw heavy bee and butterfly traffic right as many other perennials are winding down for the season. Leave the dried flower heads standing through winter for structure and wildlife cover, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep them vigorous.

common_name: Franz Schubert Phlox (Lilac-Lavender Tall Garden Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; space at least 18 inches apart for good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade with good air circulation between plants. Franz Schubert bears large, rounded flower heads in soft lilac-lavender with a subtle darker eye, a gentler, old-fashioned color that pairs well with pinks and blues in a summer border. It shares the classic tall garden phlox fragrance, carrying a light sweet scent through the border on warm evenings, and blooms over a long stretch from midsummer into early fall. Like most Phlox paniculata cultivars it is more prone to powdery mildew than resistant selections such as David or Jeana, so give it full sun, steady moisture, and generous spacing, and consider afternoon shade in the hottest Gulf South gardens where it performs best as a shorter-lived perennial.

common_name: Eva Cullum Phlox (Clear Pink Red-Eyed Garden Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; space at least 18 inches apart for good air circulation, since Eva Cullum has better mildew resistance than most older pink phlox but still benefits from open airflow.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade with good air circulation between plants. Eva Cullum produces large, fragrant flower heads in a clear, true pink centered with a small red eye, a crisp combination that holds its color well through the heat of summer without fading or muddying. It is noted among tall garden phlox cultivars for above-average resistance to powdery mildew, staying cleaner and more attractive into fall than many older pink selections, though it still benefits from full sun and generous spacing. Deadhead spent flower heads to extend bloom and prevent unwanted seedlings, which typically revert to a muddy magenta rather than coming true to the parent's clear pink.
